findings.title: SQL Injection in id at https://demo.vulnerable.example/product?id=1
findings.summary: The id parameter is concatenated into a SQL query. A crafted value changes the meaning of the query, exposing the database behind https://demo.vulnerable.example/product?id=1.
findings.reproduction: Send a GET request to https://demo.vulnerable.example/product?id=1 with id=1' OR '1'='1 and compare the response against a benign value.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries so id is bound as a value and never parsed as SQL.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery in the request body at https://demo.vulnerable.example/account/email
findings.summary: The endpoint at https://demo.vulnerable.example/account/email performs a state change without verifying the request originated from the application itself.
findings.reproduction: Host a page that auto-submits a POST to https://demo.vulnerable.example/account/email, then load it while authenticated; the change is applied.
findings.remediation: Require an unpredictable per-session token on state-changing requests and set SameSite on the session cookie.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference in invoice_id at https://demo.vulnerable.example/invoice
findings.summary: The invoice_id value selects a record without checking that the authenticated user owns it, so any user can read another user data via https://demo.vulnerable.example/invoice.
findings.reproduction: Authenticate, then request https://demo.vulnerable.example/invoice with invoice_id set to an identifier belonging to a different user.
findings.remediation: Check the authenticated user owns the referenced object on every request (IDOR). Check ownership server-side on every request rather than trusting the identifier supplied by the client.

findings.title: Reflected XSS in q at https://demo.vulnerable.example/search
findings.summary: Input supplied in q is reflected into the response without encoding, so an attacker-supplied script executes in a victim browser. This corresponds to [UNVERIFIED REFERENCE REMOVED].
findings.reproduction: Request https://demo.vulnerable.example/search with q=<svg onload=alert(1)> and observe the payload rendered unencoded in the HTML body.
findings.remediation: Encode output for the context it lands in, and prefer textContent over innerHTML when inserting untrusted text.

findings.title: Verbose Error Message in id at https://demo.vulnerable.example/product
findings.cwe_name: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
findings.summary: An unhandled error at https://demo.vulnerable.example/product returns a stack trace, disclosing framework version and server file paths that assist further attacks.
findings.reproduction: Request https://demo.vulnerable.example/product with id=id=abc to trigger the error and observe the trace in the response body.
findings.remediation: Return a generic error to the client and log the detail server-side only.
